Definition: probably akin to G138; to trail:--drag, draw, hale.
BiblicalUsage: As for Saul, he makes havoc of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women, committing them to prison, and at Lystra Jews come from Antioch and Iconium, persuade the people, and having stoned Paul, draw him out of the city, supposing he is dead. The dragging is persecution's own word: Saul drags Christians to prison, and a mob drags Paul's body out of the city, and the same hands that drag are the hands God will one day stop.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the draggers of God's people are dragging against God Himself, and I believe the man dragged out for dead at Lystra rose to walk again.
